key_concepts: Flowers contain male and female reproductive parts
The stamen is the male reproductive part made of an anther and filament
The anther produces pollen, which contains male sex cells
The pistil is the female reproductive part made of the stigma, style, and ovary
The ovary contains ovules, which contain female sex cells
Sepals are small green leaf-like structures that protect the developing flower bud
Pollen can be carried by wind from one flower to another
Pollen germinates on the stigma and grows a pollen tube to reach the egg
Fertilized ovules develop into a plant embryo contained in a seed
Pollination can be self-pollination or cross-pollination
Flowers may be adapted for insect pollination or wind pollination
